payload.reason: One proposal (practice), selected as the core and checked against the survey, the three attempt-2 spike results and the answered questions Q-169, Q-175, Q-197 and Q-198. The one fork that forced a re-synthesis, O-017, was settled by two go verdicts. Nothing in this design is blocked. What remains is person-run and is filed.
payload.selection_rationale:
Only one proposal came in, so there was nothing to choose between. It was tested against reality.

1. **It fits the code as it is.** The survey measured these seams:
   - Walk(plan, requested, parse, pathOf, open, free) at ShellReveal.cs:211, unit-tested through injected delegates.
   - The attribute read at :243-259. Today it runs after the open; this design moves it ahead of the open, inside the same try/finally that frees the pidl (:237-241).
   - RevealReason (:14-20), which gains one value.
   - FormatRevealStatus (MainWindow.xaml.cs:856-869), which gains one branch and loses the blanket hidden note.
   - No new component boundary is needed. ShellReveal.cs stays the only place that talks to the shell, as fitness.yaml:599-612 already requires for the two reveal APIs.

2. **Its one contested fork is decided by measurement, not by argument.**
   - Spike hidden-ancestor-selection-at-defaults-in-windows-sandbox went go. At fShowAllObjects=false and fShowSuperHidden=false, +H ancestors gave 18/18 and +H+S ancestors 18/18, with 0 fails.
   - Spike run-2285-control-sat-under-hidden-appdata went go on the owner's own PC. The control was selected at Hidden=2 with +H AppData four levels up.
   - So the ancestor walk the fork-decider described is not built.

3. **The behaviour is the person's decision.**
   - Q-175 (human): refuse, open nothing, name the setting, never change it, keep volume roots exempt.
   - Q-198: until the owner edits the record, that note is the agreed C-004 behaviour.
   - Q-169: no Explorer COM automation in the shipped exe.
   - The brief's 'parent-only' wording predates these answers, and the answers win.

4. **It is the simplest thing that works.** One read-only settings call, made only for Hidden targets. No caching, no ancestor reads, no confirmation after the fact, no settings write. The designer set over_engineering_flag false and named the ancestor walk as the bigger build left out. The verdicts back that judgement.

**Changes from the proposal, made against reality** (detailed in coherence_check):
- The architecture rules are defined concretely here, and build reconciles them with whatever attempt 1 left in fitness.yaml.
- The real-system-item Fact never skips.
- A case for a deny-all folder (one the user cannot open) is added.
- ProgramData\Microsoft (System-only) at defaults is recorded as measured, not predicted.
- The NoExplorerViewMember mutant is required.
- View is null when it was not read.
- The KnownWorkarounds question is settled explicitly.
- Q-197's known-limit note is added.

components.name: Visibility gate in ShellReveal.Walk
components.responsibility:
After resolve-back (ShellReveal.cs:230-231) and before the open (:233), Walk reads the target's own attributes with File.GetAttributes on the \\?\ path. The read moves up from :243-259, keeps the volume-root exemption, and still treats an exception as 'not hidden'.

Only for a Hidden target that is not a volume root, Walk calls the explorer delegate once. If ExplorerView.Shows(hidden, system) is false, it returns Failed / HiddenByExplorerSettings with HResult 0 and HiddenBy and View set, and never calls open.

Ancestors are never read, because O-017 settled on own attributes only. A +H file inside a +H folder is refused like any other Hidden item; Sandbox X1 measured that Explorer would open the folder with nothing selected.

Build records one mutation check: delete the gate, see the H-only (0,0) theory row fail, then restore byte for byte (SL-020 lesson).
components.key_interactions:
Order of checks: NameUnaddressable, then parse failure (NoLongerExists or None), then ParsedAsAnotherItem, then the new refusal, then open failure, then Exact.

The gate sits inside the try whose finally frees the pidl, so the pidl is freed exactly once on the refusal path too. RevealAsync passes the effective-view reader. Hidden and System stay on the outcome for both kinds.

components.name: ExplorerView, reader and hide-only override
components.responsibility:
- ExplorerView(ShowsHidden, ShowsProtected) with Shows(hidden, system) = !hidden || (ShowsHidden && (!system || ShowsProtected)).
- FromShellState(uint) reads bit 0 (fShowAllObjects) and bit 15 (fShowSuperHidden) only.
- ReadExplorerView() calls SHGetSetSettings with a zeroed buffer of at least 64 bytes, mask 0x00040001 (SSF_SHOWALLOBJECTS | SSF_SHOWSUPERHIDDEN) and bSet=false. It is read fresh at each hidden reveal, with no cache.
- internal static OverrideExplorerView(ExplorerView? mask): once set, the effective view is real AND mask, field by field, and null clears it. No mask can turn a refusal into an Exact.
- The override is set once before Main and read on the reveal STA thread, so it is published with Volatile.Write/Read.
components.key_interactions: ShellReveal.cs is the only src file that names SHGetSetSettings or OverrideExplorerView (twinned rule A). The hook reaches the override by reflection, the way it reaches FailListingOf. The P/Invoke never passes true for bSet (twinned rule B).

components.name: RevealOutcome shape
components.responsibility:
RevealKind stays {Exact, Failed}. RevealReason gains HiddenByExplorerSettings.

RevealOutcome gains:
- HiddenBy, a [Flags] value {None, HiddenFiles, ProtectedFiles}. HiddenFiles = Hidden && !ShowsHidden. ProtectedFiles = Hidden && System && !ShowsProtected.
- View, an ExplorerView? holding the effective view used. It is null when no view was read (non-hidden target, volume root, or an earlier failure), so a log reader cannot mistake 'not read' for 'nothing shown'.

There is no hiding-ancestor field.
components.key_interactions: Read by MainWindow.FormatRevealStatus, the hook's reveal record (RevealMode.cs OutcomeEntry), R-002/R-003 and ShellRevealTests.

components.name: Reveal status line
components.responsibility:
FormatRevealStatus (MainWindow.xaml.cs:856-869) gets a new HiddenByExplorerSettings branch: "Nothing was opened: Explorer hides '<leaf>' (<label>[; <label>])."
- HiddenFiles gives the label 'Don't show hidden files, folders, or drives'.
- ProtectedFiles gives 'Hide protected operating system files'.
- Both give both labels, HiddenFiles first.

Exact always gives an empty string, so the line collapses (:832). The old Exact+Hidden note is deleted. NoLongerExists and 'Couldn't show…' are unchanged.

Build checks the label texts on this PC by resolving the Folder Options strings read-only (see outside_claims) and records them in the design note.
components.key_interactions: RevealStatus is a single trimmed line; the proposal cites MainWindow.xaml:144-148 for NoWrap and CharacterEllipsis, unverified by the survey. The outcome and leaf come first, so the ellipsis cuts only the tail of the labels. The tooltip carries the full text.

components.name: Core unit tests
components.responsibility:
1. A theory over real temp items (plain, S-only, H-only, H+S; file and folder; one H-only item at more than 260 characters) × the four injected views. It checks Kind, Reason, HiddenBy, View, how often the delegate is called (0 for non-hidden, otherwise 1), how often open is called (once only for Exact), and that free is called once. It replaces Walk_HiddenAndSystemAttributes_DetectedOnExactItem (:222-245).
2. Non-hidden items inside a +H temp folder and inside a +H+S temp folder at (0,0): Exact, delegate never called.
3. A temp folder with +H+S and a deny-all ACE for the current user, inside a readable parent: refused. The ACE is reset in cleanup.
4. A real-item Fact: C:\System Volume Information always, plus every H+S *.sys at the system drive root, through the real parse and pathOf with a recording open stub, at injected (1,0): Failed / ProtectedFiles and no open. It never skips; if no *.sys is found, it says so in the test output and still asserts System Volume Information.
5. Volume-root exemption.
6. Precedence of the earlier failures.
7. FromShellState table.
8. Override AND over every real × mask pair, plus null.
9. Read-only cross-check of ReadExplorerView against HKCU on this PC.
components.key_interactions: Uses the existing parse/pathOf/open/free seams plus the explorer delegate. Nothing writes Explorer settings. The real-item Fact runs the real parse on an STA thread, as the existing reveal tests do.

components.name: Hook arming, reveal record and mutant
components.responsibility:
FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW='<hidden>|<protected>' (each 0 or 1) is armed in StartupHook.Initialize beside ArmFailListing. On success it logs 'explorer-view-injected injected=a|b'.

Every failure logs 'explorer-view refused reason=format|type|member|invoke' and throws out of Initialize, so the exe ends before Main and no reveal is clicked. The variable is added to the hook's mode/variable list.

The reveal record (RevealMode.cs OutcomeEntry) gains hiddenBy, the injected view and the effective view.

A required mutant, NoExplorerViewMember, follows the pattern of NoFailListingMember: it touches the ValidateSet, $CaseMutants, the $names roster and the MayFail key, so R-003 must notice when the override member is gone.
components.key_interactions: RevealMode.cs is in the same folder; the mutant lives in tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1. The proposal's line references here (StartupHook.cs:226, :250-277, :291, :313-317, :373-375; RevealMode.cs:456-488) were not measured by the survey, so build confirms them. Q-114: a slice touching FsaWindowHook/** and WindowCases.ps1 runs WindowMutants -Mutant All at validate.

components.name: R-003 window case and R-002 pin move
components.responsibility:
Injected-defaults step, safe to run unattended:
- Run with FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW=0|0.
- Reveal temp H-only and H+S files and folders, and the paging file found at the system root.
- Assert Kind=Failed, the reason, hiddenBy, the exact status text and the 'explorer-view-injected' line, and that no new Shell.Application window appeared.
- A malformed-value sub-step expects the refused line and no reveal record.

Settings-in-force step:
- Read HKCU Explorer\Advanced Hidden and ShowSuperHidden read-only, before and after; if they changed, the run is void.
- Derive each target's expectation from the predicate.
- Click only targets whose expectation is a refusal (at this PC's (1,0): the H+S items, giving ProtectedFiles only). Skip Exact targets and report them owed to a person.

R-002's hs_file.sys pin (:3781-3782, kind 'Exact' plus a regex on the old note) moves to the derived expectation.
components.key_interactions: Uses Invoke-RevealRun (no --report), Shell.Application window reading and Close-CaseWindows. No step changes Explorer settings (settled rule C). Steps that would land stay person-run; Q-176's exception covered SL-089 only.

components.name: B-007/B-008 layout pins
components.responsibility:
Re-pin the FSA_HOOK_STATUS texts at WindowCases.ps1:2150, 2206 and 4360 (measured to pin the old pagefile.sys note) to the longest new text: both labels with a 200-character leaf.

The existing minimum-size runs carry the layout check. At 560x644 they log RevealStatus's DesiredSize width against its ActualWidth, so what is cut is on record.
components.key_interactions: Size mode through FSA_HOOK_STATUS. The one-line ellipsis status keeps every list's full-row floor (Q-049).

components.name: Architecture rules and their twins
components.responsibility:
Rules A and B (src/**/*.cs) are twinned:
- a verbatim @"..." Fact each in ArchitectureRulesTests;
- yaml entries above the first '# settled by SL-' marker, single-quoted, with (?m) and including_comments: true;
- must-fire plant rows whose anchors are whole stripped source lines, with also_settled where the planted file is guarded more than once.
Build runs harness.py --only <ids> and expects AS-RECORDED, and runs rules-parity, which must AGREE with the new counts.

Rule C (tests/window/**) is settled.

Reconciliation: after acceptance, .taad/fitness.yaml holds exactly one '# settled by SL-091' block, containing rule C only.
- The engine's appended copies of A and B move above the first marker.
- Any SL-091 block left by attempt 1 that this design does not declare is replaced. The proposal places such a block at :1126-1131; the survey's grep found no SHGetSetSettings in fitness.yaml at 36b461d, so it may not exist.
- Build runs tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-001 (about 3 s) and fixes any literal count pin it turns red (the silent-red failure of SL-044..047).
components.key_interactions: Also tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ArchitectureRulesTests.cs, eng/rules-harness/plants.json and RuleCopiesAgreeTests. harness.py's known 'unable' verdict (import rule UNRAN) is expected; plant outcomes are judged with --only.

components.name: SL-091 design note
components.key_interactions: Read by reviewers in place of C-004's old clause (Q-198), and by the person for the sitting.

key_decisions.decision: A Hidden or Hidden+System item that Explorer's settings hide is refused: nothing is opened, the status line names the setting, and Explorer's settings are never changed (Q-175, Q-198). This replaces the brief's and derived criteria C2-C4's 'parent-only' wording. Validate should read C2-C4 as 'not reported as landing, setting named, nothing opened'.
key_decisions.rationale: Q-175 is a human decision and Q-198 confirms 'opens nothing' as the agreed C-004 behaviour. No measurement contradicts them. Opening the parent instead would be one branch and one text. The failure that affects the owner today is covered too: H+S at (1,0) is reported Exact while 0 of 8 were selected, and it is now refused with ProtectedFiles.

key_decisions.decision: The predicate reads only the item's own attributes. No ancestor walk is built (O-017 settled).
key_decisions.rationale:
Two go verdicts:
- Sandbox, real ShellReveal, at fShowAllObjects=false and fShowSuperHidden=false: +H ancestors 18/18, +H+S ancestors 18/18, 0 fails, controls landing.
- Run 2285 on the owner's PC: the control was selected at Hidden=2 under +H AppData.
The verdict outranks argument. The host residual (26200, Medium-integrity Explorer, +H direct parent, +H+S ancestors) is filed for the person. If that sitting shows blocking, the affected class gets the ancestor rule in a new design. That would be a data-model change, which is why it is recorded here rather than guessed.

key_decisions.decision: RevealOutcome gains HiddenBy {HiddenFiles, ProtectedFiles} and a nullable View. RevealKind stays two values. No ancestor field.
key_decisions.rationale: This contract has four consumers (MainWindow, the hook's reveal record, R-002/R-003, Core tests). A nullable View keeps 'not read' apart from 'nothing shown' in logs.

key_decisions.decision: Explorer's view is read with SHGetSetSettings(0x00040001, bSet=false) at each hidden reveal: read-only, uncached, and only for Hidden targets.
key_decisions.rationale: Q-175 names this API. On this PC it answers and agrees with the registry. Reading only for Hidden targets keeps plain reveals free of shell-state reads. If the filed mid-session spike shows stale reads, the fallback is a read-only HKCU read behind the same delegate, with no contract change.

key_decisions.decision: The test override is hide-only (effective = real AND mask), armed before Main, and fails closed. The NoExplorerViewMember mutant is required, not optional.
key_decisions.rationale: An injected view can then only produce refusals, so unattended R-003 clicks never open Explorer. The dangerous shape is a renamed member leaving the override unarmed while R-003 clicks under the real view, and only a mutant shows the fail-closed throw fires for it.

key_decisions.decision: The status text leads with 'Nothing was opened' and the leaf, then the Folder Options label(s). The old blanket Exact+Hidden note is deleted, so Exact means Explorer will select the item.
key_decisions.rationale: RevealStatus is one trimmed line, so the tail is what gets cut. The build check showed the old note appeared whatever the settings were, including when the item was selected (this PC, H-only, 5/5).

key_decisions.decision: Rules A and B over src are twinned. Rule C over tests/window is settled. fitness.yaml ends with exactly one SL-091 settled block, whatever attempt 1 left.
key_decisions.rationale: Build cannot run Fitness (SL-071), so twinning lets dotnet test catch a second settings reader or a settings write during build. All patterns are single-line, so xUnit's per-line match and Fitness's whole-file match agree (SL-087). The tests/window rule guards tooling that validate's Fitness check reads, so a twin adds little.

key_decisions.decision: Window steps whose expected outcome is a landing are never clicked unattended; they skip and report themselves owed to a person. Layout is checked by the existing B-007/B-008 pins, not inside R-003.
key_decisions.rationale: A landing opens a real Explorer window, and Q-176's exception covered SL-089 only. Reveal runs have no --report, so B-007/B-008 through FSA_HOOK_STATUS are the existing layout check.

key_decisions.decision: The refusal is not a KnownWorkarounds entry and gets no checkbox.
key_decisions.rationale: Explorer not selecting a hidden item is Explorer obeying the person's own view setting. That is designed behaviour, not an outside defect. The false success was this project's own defect (Exact from hr==0), and it is fixed, not toggled. Refusing rather than opening the parent is the person's product decision (Q-175). An 'off' position could only restore the project's own false report.

key_decisions.decision: Ship on Windows 11 26200 measurements with the limit stated (Q-197). Hand the C-004 replacement text to the owner (Q-198).
key_decisions.rationale: Both are decided answers. No Windows 10 machine is available, and no stage can edit the architecture record (Q-125).

payload.coherence_check:
One proposal, so there is no composition to check. Nothing in this design has yet survived a disagreement with another designer; the reviewer is the first to argue with it.

**Checked instead, against reality:**

(1) **Against the survey's measured code.**
- The gate, the reason value and the status branch land at the seams the survey read: ShellReveal.cs:211, 217-261, 237-241; MainWindow.xaml.cs:832, 856-869; pins at WindowCases.ps1:2150, 2206, 4360, 3781-3782; fitness.yaml:599-612.
- The proposal's other line references were not measured by the survey: StartupHook.cs:226/250-277/291/313-317/373-375, RevealMode.cs:456-488, WindowCases.ps1:3370-3372, MainWindow.xaml:144-148, fitness.yaml:1126-1131 and taad3 fitness.py:365. They are carried as the designer's and build confirms them.

(2) **One contradiction found, and the seam redesigned.**
- The proposal assumes attempt 1 left a settled SL-091 block at fitness.yaml:1126-1131, containing rules '3 and 4' whose text this proposal never states.
- The survey's grep found SHGetSetSettings nowhere in .taad/fitness.yaml, and the take-back happened at 36b461d, the survey's own HEAD. So that block may not exist.
- This design therefore defines all three rules concretely. It merges the proposal's two tests/ rules into one settled tests/window rule, and makes build reconcile fitness.yaml to exactly one SL-091 settled block, whatever is there.

(3) **Against the answered questions.**
- Q-175 and Q-198 (refuse, open nothing) override the brief's and C2-C4's 'parent-only'. That is said plainly in key_decisions.
- Q-169's 'says it opened the parent folder' is superseded by the newer human Q-175.
- No answered question contradicts a measurement.

(4) **Against the spikes.**
- The ancestor fork follows the two go verdicts and is not reopened.
- The proposal listed System-only at defaults as predicted. The Sandbox measured it: ProgramData\Microsoft is System-only and was selected 6/6. The predicate table is corrected.

(5) **Against project rules.**
- The proposal's 'skip with a message' for a missing paging file would sit near the Skip patterns of CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped and could pass silently. The Fact now never skips and always asserts System Volume Information.
- 'default when no view was read' would read as (false,false), which looks like Windows defaults. View is now nullable.

(6) **Gaps added.**
- A case for an item the user cannot open: SL-088's own target, and the branch where an attribute-read exception turns into a false Exact.
- The fail-closed mutant is now required.

(7) **Workaround rule:** checked, and found not to apply (see key_decisions).

(8) **No stack choice was needed.** Everything sits inside the declared C#, .NET 10, WPF, xUnit and hook stack.

decidable_disagreements is empty on purpose. The one fork was settled by measurement. The host-only residual is filed for the person rather than raised as a fork, because the verdict outranks reopening it.

contracts.name: ShellReveal.Walk(plan, requested, parse, pathOf, open, free, explorer)
contracts.notes:
explorer is a Func<ExplorerView>. It is called at most once, after resolve-back, only for a Hidden target that is not a volume root. Only the target's own attributes decide; ancestors are never read.

When the target is refused, Walk returns Kind=Failed, Reason=HiddenByExplorerSettings, HResult=0, HiddenBy set and View set, and open is never called. An Exact outcome carries View only if the target was Hidden.
contracts.error_cases:
- If the attribute read throws, the target is treated as not hidden (unchanged).
- NameUnaddressable, NoLongerExists and ParsedAsAnotherItem keep precedence, and the delegate is not called for them.
- An open failure after a visible verdict gives Failed / None with that hr.
- The pidl is freed exactly once on every path.
contracts.auth_model: Ordinary user, no elevation. Reads file attributes and per-user shell state only.

contracts.name: ReadExplorerView / FromShellState / OverrideExplorerView
contracts.notes:
Read: SHGetSetSettings(zeroed buffer of at least 64 bytes, 0x00040001, bSet=false). ShowsHidden is bit 0 and ShowsProtected is bit 15 of the first DWORD. Read fresh at each hidden reveal.

Override (internal, process-wide, set before Main): effective = real AND mask, field by field. Null clears it. It can only hide, never reveal.
contracts.error_cases: SHGetSetSettings returns void, so a failure cannot be detected. A wrong bit-15 decode most likely refuses, the conservative direction, because 0 is the only value observed. No code path writes.

contracts.name: ExplorerView.Shows(hidden, system) predicate table
contracts.notes:
visible = !hidden || (ShowsHidden && (!system || ShowsProtected)).

Measured:
- (1,0): plain, System-only (8/8) and H-only (5/5) selected; H+S not selected (0/8).
- (2,0): H and H+S not selected (0/13, run 2285, hr 0, parent opened, no dialog).
- (2,0): System-only selected (Sandbox, ProgramData\Microsoft, 6/6).
- (2,0): non-hidden items under +H or +H+S ancestors selected (Sandbox, 18/18 each; host run 2285 with +H four levels up).
- (2,0): a +H file in a +H folder opens that folder with nothing selected (Sandbox, 3/3).

Predicted:
- (1,1): H+S selected.
- (2,1): H and H+S not selected.
contracts.error_cases: On host 26200 with a Medium-integrity Explorer, the +H direct-parent and +H+S ancestor rows are not measured; they are filed for the person. (1,1) is the only cell where the predicate claims Exact without measurement.

contracts.name: Reveal status line text
contracts.notes:
- Exact: empty, so the line collapses.
- HiddenByExplorerSettings: "Nothing was opened: Explorer hides '<leaf>' (<label>[; <label>])." Labels: 'Don't show hidden files, folders, or drives' (HiddenFiles) and 'Hide protected operating system files' (ProtectedFiles). HiddenFiles comes first when both apply.
- NoLongerExists and 'Couldn't show…' are unchanged.
The label strings are checked by build against this PC's own Folder Options strings.
contracts.error_cases: On the single NoWrap line, the ellipsis may cut the label tail at 560 px. The outcome and leaf come first, and the tooltip holds the full text.

contracts.name: FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW hook failpoint
contracts.notes: Value '<hidden>|<protected>', each 0 or 1. Armed in Initialize before Main, beside FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING. It logs 'explorer-view-injected injected=a|b', and every reveal record carries hiddenBy plus the injected and effective views. Because of the AND, an injected view can only produce refusals.
contracts.error_cases: A bad format, missing type, missing member or invoke error logs 'explorer-view refused reason=…' and throws out of Initialize. The exe ends before Main, so no reveal is clicked.

contracts.name: R-002 / R-003 reveal expectations
contracts.notes:
- Injected 0|0 step: refusals only, no new Shell.Application window, exact text, and the injected line present.
- Settings-in-force step: expectations come from HKCU read-only, before and after. Refusal targets are clicked; Exact targets are skipped and reported owed to a person.
- R-002's hs_file.sys pin follows the derived expectation: Failed / ProtectedFiles at this PC's (1,0).
contracts.error_cases: If the settings change between the before and after reads, the run is void and says so. No step changes Explorer settings.

architecture_rules.name: only ShellReveal.cs reads or overrides Explorer's view settings
architecture_rules.because:
Walk's visibility verdict, its precedence and the hook's hide-only AND are all applied inside ShellReveal. A second reader elsewhere in src would decide on its own what Explorer shows, outside the override, and could report a landing Walk would refuse. That is the false success this slice removes.

Twinned: a verbatim Fact plus a yaml entry above the first '# settled by SL-' marker, with (?m) and including_comments: true, so dotnet test catches it during build, which cannot run Fitness.

architecture_rules.name: the app never writes Explorer's settings
architecture_rules.because:
Q-169, Q-175 and the brief: the app reads Explorer's view state and never changes it. A reveal that switched Hidden or ShowSuperHidden to make itself land would change the person's machine behind their back.

Twinned like rule A. Every pattern stays on one line ([^;\r\n], [ \t]) so xUnit's per-line match agrees with Fitness's whole-file match (SL-087). With including_comments on, no comment may put SHGetSetSettings and the word true on one line.

architecture_rules.name: no window case or hook changes Explorer's view settings
architecture_rules.because:
Only a person may change Explorer's Hidden setting. R-003 asserts refusals through the hook's hide-only injection precisely so that nothing unattended needs the real setting changed. A case that set Hidden=2 itself would change the owner's desktop, and if killed mid-run would leave it changed.

Settled rather than twinned: it guards test tooling that validate's Fitness check reads, and the hook is outside FsAnalyser.slnx. It is a name-based tripwire, so a registry path held in a variable is not caught.

cases.shape: the item itself is not Hidden: a plain file or folder, or a System-only one
cases.why: Walk must reach the open without reading Explorer's settings. A gate that refused on System alone would refuse folders like ProgramData\Microsoft, which Explorer selects at defaults (Sandbox 6/6) and at the owner's settings (spike-91 cell 0, 8/8).
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ShellReveal". Theory rows plain and S-only × file and folder × all four injected views: Kind=Exact, explorer delegate called 0 times, open called once, View null.

cases.shape: the item is not Hidden but a folder above it is +H, or +H+S
cases.why: O-017 settled on own attributes only. A Walk that consulted ancestors would refuse every reveal under AppData at Windows defaults, which Explorer selects (Sandbox 18/18 per class; run 2285's control).
cases.check: Same dotnet test filter. A Fact puts a plain file and a plain folder inside a +H temp folder and inside a +H+S temp folder, at injected (0,0): Exact, delegate called 0 times.

cases.shape: the item is Hidden (not System) and hidden files are not shown, including a +H file directly inside a +H folder and an item at more than 260 characters
cases.why: Run 2285: 0 of 13 selected, hr 0, parent opened. Walk's current Exact from S_OK is the false success this slice removes. The refusal path must also free the pidl and never call open.
cases.check: Same dotnet test filter. Theory rows H-only × (0,0) and (0,1): Failed / HiddenByExplorerSettings, HiddenBy=HiddenFiles, HResult 0, open called 0 times, free called once.

cases.shape: the item is Hidden but every setting that would hide it is set to show: H-only at (1,x), H+S at (1,1)
cases.why: On the owner's PC (1,0), H-only items are selected 5 of 5. Refusing them would break a reveal that works today. Exact must now leave the status line empty, so the old blanket note has to be gone.
cases.check: Same dotnet test filter. Theory rows: Exact, delegate called once, open called once. Also Select-String -Path src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs -SimpleMatch 'only highlights it if' returns nothing.

cases.shape: the item is Hidden+System and protected operating-system files are hidden: at the owner's (1,0), and at Windows defaults (0,0)
cases.why: This is the failure affecting the owner today: H+S 0 of 8 at (1,0) while Walk reports Exact. At (0,0) both settings hide it, so both flags must be set.
cases.check: Same dotnet test filter. Theory rows H+S × (1,0): HiddenBy=ProtectedFiles. H+S × (0,0) and (0,1): HiddenBy includes HiddenFiles, and includes ProtectedFiles where ShowsProtected is false. Open called 0 times in every row.

cases.shape: the item is one the user cannot open: a temp folder carrying +H+S with a deny-all ACE inside a readable parent, the real C:\System Volume Information, and the paging file at the system drive root
cases.why: These are SL-088's own targets. If the attribute read throws, the catch marks the item not hidden and Walk reports a false Exact. U-107 shows a file's attributes come through the parent's list right; folders and System Volume Information are not measured.
cases.check: Same dotnet test filter. A Fact with the deny-all temp folder (ACE set for the current user's SID, reset in cleanup), and a real-item Fact for System Volume Information plus every H+S *.sys found, through the real parse and pathOf with a recording open stub, at injected (1,0): Failed / ProtectedFiles, open called 0 times. Neither Fact ever skips.

cases.shape: the target is a volume root (C:\), whose own attributes can read Hidden+System
cases.why: Without the exemption, every drive reveal would be refused at any setting.
cases.check: Same dotnet test filter. A Fact with Walk on C:\ at injected (0,0): Exact, delegate called 0 times, View null.

cases.shape: an earlier failure applies to a hidden target: it no longer exists, it parses as another item, or its name is unaddressable
cases.why: The gate sits after resolve-back. Reporting HiddenByExplorerSettings for a vanished item would lose the 'Rescan to refresh' advice, and reading the settings there is wasted.
cases.check: Same dotnet test filter. Facts give NoLongerExists, ParsedAsAnotherItem and NameUnaddressable, each with delegate called 0 times and the pidl freed once wherever one was created.

cases.shape: the shell-state DWORD carries bits other than 0 and 15 (0x5 on this PC, 0x8 in the Sandbox), or bit 15 (0x8000, 0x8001)
cases.why: Neighbouring flags such as fShowSysFiles must not be read as 'shows protected files'. The real read on this PC must agree with HKCU, or every expectation derived from the registry is wrong.
cases.check: Same dotnet test filter. A FromShellState table Fact (0x0, 0x1, 0x5, 0x8, 0x8000, 0x8001) plus a read-only Fact that ReadExplorerView matches HKCU Explorer\Advanced (ShowsHidden == (Hidden==1), ShowsProtected == (ShowSuperHidden==1)).

cases.behaviour: inject a view for a test
cases.shape: a test override is set: every real × injected pair, and null
cases.why: If an injection could widen the view, an unattended R-003 click would land and open Explorer. The AND makes injections refusal-only by construction.
cases.check: Same dotnet test filter. A Fact over 4×4 pairs: effective == real AND mask; any refusal under the real view stays a refusal under every mask; null restores the real view.

cases.behaviour: show a refused reveal on the status line
cases.shape: each label variant: HiddenFiles only (H-only at injected 0|0), both (H+S at injected 0|0), ProtectedFiles only (H+S under this PC's (1,0) settings in force)
cases.why: FormatRevealStatus's new branch maps HiddenBy to Folder Options labels. A refusal must open nothing, and a target expected to land must never be clicked unattended.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case R-003. Asserts kind, reason, hiddenBy, exact text, the 'explorer-view-injected' line and no new Shell.Application window. The settings-in-force step reports any Exact-expected target as owed, not clicked.

cases.shape: FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW is malformed, or the OverrideExplorerView member cannot be found
cases.why: An unarmed override would let R-003 click reveals under the real view. On a PC that shows hidden files, that lands and opens Explorer unattended.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case R-003 (malformed sub-step expects 'explorer-view refused reason=format' and no reveal record). Then pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant NoExplorerViewMember, where R-003 must fail with the member reason.

cases.behaviour: show the longest refusal at the minimum window size
cases.shape: both labels with a 200-character leaf at 560x644
cases.why: RevealStatus must stay one ellipsis line, or it takes rows from the lists (SL-047's 24 px allowance, Q-049). The pins at 2150/2206/4360 still hold the old note.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case B-007, then -Case B-008, with the re-pinned FSA_HOOK_STATUS. The log records RevealStatus DesiredSize against ActualWidth.

cases.shape: the attribute read throws (the item is deleted between the parse and the read)
cases.why: Not worth a test: this existing branch treats the item as not hidden and goes on to the open. A deleted target makes that open fail or open the parent, a race the parse's NoLongerExists check already narrows. There is no deterministic seam without injecting the attribute read, which this design deliberately does not add.

outside_claims.claim: SHGetSetSettings with SSF_SHOWALLOBJECTS | SSF_SHOWSUPERHIDDEN and bSet=false answers read-only on this PC, and its fShowAllObjects agrees with HKCU Explorer\Advanced Hidden=1.
outside_claims.source: Survey: read-only probe, flags=0x00000005, Hidden=1, ShowSuperHidden=0
outside_claims.if_wrong: The gate would decide from a value Explorer does not use.

outside_claims.claim: In the SHELLSTATE filled by SHGetSetSettings, fShowAllObjects is bit 0 and fShowSuperHidden is bit 15 of the first DWORD. The function returns void.
outside_claims.source: memory (shlobj_core.h SHELLSTATE bitfield). Bit 0 is consistent with this PC (0x5 at Hidden=1) and the Sandbox (0x8 at Hidden=2); bit 15 only ever seen at 0.
outside_claims.if_wrong: ShowsProtected would be mis-decoded. Most likely it reads 0 and refuses H+S items Explorer would show; a mis-read 1 would claim landings for H+S.

outside_claims.claim: At Hidden=2 / ShowSuperHidden=0, SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems on a Hidden or Hidden+System item returns S_OK and opens the parent with nothing selected, with no dialog and no elevation.
outside_claims.source: Person's hand run 2285 (0/13, hr=0x00000000, folderOk=True), read from the engine record by spike run-2285-control-sat-under-hidden-appdata
outside_claims.if_wrong: If Explorer did select at defaults, the refusal would block reveals that would land.

outside_claims.claim: At Hidden=1 / ShowSuperHidden=0, H-only items are selected (5/5), H+S items are not (0/8), and System-only items are selected (8/8).
outside_claims.if_wrong: The owner's own reveals would be refused or falsely reported as landing.

outside_claims.claim: At defaults, whether Explorer selects an item depends only on the item's own attributes: non-hidden items under +H or +H+S ancestors are selected, and System-only ProgramData\Microsoft is selected.
outside_claims.source: Spike hidden-ancestor-selection-at-defaults-in-windows-sandbox (build 26100, High-integrity Explorer: 18/18 per class, F2 6/6); spike run-2285-control-sat-under-hidden-appdata (host, +H four levels up)
outside_claims.if_wrong: Reveals under AppData or ProgramData would be falsely reported Exact. RevealOutcome would need an ancestor field (filed host check).

outside_claims.claim: A +H file directly in a +H folder, at defaults, opens that folder with nothing selected.
outside_claims.if_wrong: Only the predicate table row changes; the item is refused on its own attribute either way.

outside_claims.claim: File.GetAttributes on an item the user cannot open succeeds when its parent can be listed, including real C:\System Volume Information and pagefile.sys.
outside_claims.source: memory; U-107 measured this for files only (file deny ACE alone gave error 0). The current note pin for pagefile.sys implies Hidden is read there. Case 6 settles folders and System Volume Information.
outside_claims.if_wrong: The catch would mark these items not hidden, and Walk would report a false Exact for exactly SL-088's targets.

outside_claims.claim: Volume roots such as C:\ can report Hidden+System in their own attributes, which is why they are exempt.
outside_claims.source: memory; the exemption already exists in Walk (survey)
outside_claims.if_wrong: Nothing breaks; the exemption is merely unnecessary.

outside_claims.claim: The Folder Options labels read 'Don't show hidden files, folders, or drives' and 'Hide protected operating system files (Recommended)'. Their text can be resolved read-only via the Text values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced\Folder\Hidden\NOHIDDEN and ...\Folder\SuperHidden with SHLoadIndirectString.
outside_claims.if_wrong: The status line would name a setting the user cannot find. Build checks the strings on this PC and corrects the text.

outside_claims.claim: SHGetSetSettings reflects a change made in Explorer while the app is running, without a restart.
outside_claims.source: memory; spike shgetsetsettings-tracks-midsession-toggle undecided (needs a person)
outside_claims.if_wrong: A toggle made while the app is open goes unseen until restart. The fallback is a read-only HKCU read behind the same delegate.

outside_claims.claim: An exception thrown from a DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS Initialize stops the app before Main runs.
outside_claims.source: memory; the proposal cites ArmFailListing as precedent in StartupHook.cs (line refs not measured)
outside_claims.if_wrong: A failed arming would leave the exe running under the real view. The NoExplorerViewMember mutant would expose it.

outside_claims.claim: Windows 11 25H2 (26200) is an enablement package on 24H2's 26100 base, so Sandbox 26100 shell filtering is close kin to the host's.
outside_claims.if_wrong: The host could differ from the Sandbox on ancestor rows. That is what the filed host sitting checks.

outside_claims.claim: Windows 10 decodes these settings and filters hidden items in Explorer the same way.
outside_claims.if_wrong: Refusals that were not needed, or reveals that land where the item cannot be seen, on Windows 10. Stated as a known limit.

taste_disagreements: The status text is composed in App code-behind (FormatRevealStatus), so its three label variants are checked only through R-003 window runs. Moving the text into Core would make them checkable by xUnit, but would split UI wording from the window.
The tests/window rule is settled rather than twinned. A twin would let dotnet test catch a settings write in a window script during build, at the cost of a Fact and parity-count churn.

The refusal is not a KnownWorkarounds entry, on the reading that Explorer obeying its own view setting is not a defect. A reviewer who reads S_OK-with-nothing-selected as an outside defect would want a checkbox, but its 'off' position could only restore this project's own false report.
Wording: "Explorer hides '<leaf>' (<label>)" versus "Explorer's settings hide '<leaf>'". The proposal's form keeps the leaf earlier on a line that gets cut.
One NoWrap ellipsis line with a tooltip, rather than a status line that wraps.

prior_art.pattern: Reveal through `explorer /select`, spawned without checking the exit code: fire-and-forget with no success signal. U-114 measured `/select` silently misrouting at 300+ characters, so this design decides from the shell's own state instead.
'Reveal in Explorer' silently opened the parent with nothing selected and gave no error: the symptom this slice stops reporting as success.
reveal_item_in_dir canonicalizes the path, then reveals, with no visibility check first in the fetched source.
ShowItemInFolder: SHParseDisplayName + SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems, falling back to opening the folder, with no hidden-setting check. This is the 'open the parent anyway' path Q-175 declined.
SHGetSetSettings with SSF_SHOWALLOBJECTS | SSF_SHOWSUPERHIDDEN is the documented read of Explorer's hidden-item view state.

Windows 11 25H2 (26200) ships as an enablement package on 24H2's 26100 servicing base, so Sandbox 26100 shell behaviour is close kin to the host's. Not proof, which is why the host run is still filed.
Ask the dispatcher's own resolution rule before a side-effecting dispatch that gives no failure signal.

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Mobile intent and URL dispatch (iOS canOpenURL, Android resolveActivity)
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: The product may not confirm a landing after the fact (Q-169, Q-175), so a check beforehand against the target's own rule is the honest option. The spikes show that rule's input is the item's own attributes alone.
